newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Phased EU enlargement will produce chaos, says Zeman.
newsitem.headline: Phased EU enlargement will produce chaos, says Zeman.

text.p: The speaker of the Czech parliament warned on Thursday there could be chaos if the countries of central and east Europe and the Baltic states did not all join the European Union at the same time.

Enlarging the EU by dribs and drabs was about as intelligent as trying to phase in a shift from driving on the left to driving on the right, for example by making passenger cars drive on the right but letting lorries continue to drive on the left, Milos Zeman told a news conference in the European Parliament.

"The model of a two-speed or a three-speed Europe should not be accepted as a model for the enlargement of the EU. The logic is unfortunately that there would be first class and second class members," Zeman said.

He was speaking at the end of a two-day meeting between the president of the European Parliament, Jose Maria Gil-Robles, and the speakers of nine of the 10 central and east European countries preparing to join the 15-member EU.

Alfreds Cepanis, the speaker of the Latvian parliament, said the applicant states wanted the EU to speed up the legislative reforms and other preparations needed before the EU could expand, but he recognised this was a sensitive process.

He declined to say whether the applicants were experiencing problems in adapting their laws to those of the EU and embracing the market economy -- essential conditions for joining the rich man's club.

The European Parliament president warned that the EU still had to put its own house in order -- reforming its decision- making process, tackling unemployment and achieving its own monetary union -- before it could think about taking in another 10 members.

Gil-Robles said he hoped the reform of the EU treaty could be completed by the June deadline, so that future meetings with the candidate country parliaments could focus more closely on specific matters, such as organised crime or the construction of trans-European transport, energy and information networks.

Ivan Gasparovic, the leader of the Slovak assembly, said cooperation and coordination between the EU and its prospective new members would be greatly improved if observers from the east European parliaments could sit in on the European Parliament committees preparing new EU legislation.
At the moment, he said, the EU was taking decisions affecting the applicant countries "which are not based on objective foundations."
